final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor did not provide genuinely new admissible evidence; the response mainly reframed the same record more narrowly and conceded key weaknesses already identified. That narrower position is important to characterize correctly: it rejects the overbroad claim that controls alone make certification compliant, but it does not supply the missing evidence needed to move the packet to compliant_with_caveats. On the summary-only record, the exposed supply-chain vendor-screening segment remains in scope, remains below target, is not covered by approved risk acceptance, and there is still no admissible proof that the required pre-launch disclosure artifact exists and satisfies policy. Because the unresolved issue is an actual compliance predicate rather than a mere wording problem, caveated treatment is not yet evidentially supported from the admissible record alone.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows that explicit pre-launch disclosure of the supply-chain vendor-screening limitation was actually completed.
No admissible evidence shows the affected use case was excluded from rollout.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance explicitly covering the exposed segment.
The policy text states rollout controls and post-launch monitoring do not cure disclosure duties while the affected segment remains exposed.
The actor's narrower framing is analytically better, but it is still not backed by the missing compliance predicate: proof of disclosure satisfying policy.
